You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>
Give the answer even when some details remain uncertain. Do not output a long reasoning trace.

Based on the chest X-ray findings presented in the figures, which of the following statements best describes the changes observed from pre-operative to post-operative status in this patient with a right upper lobe bronchial carcinoid?

A) The mass in the right upper lobe bronchus appears larger in Figure 3 compared to Figure 1a, and post-operatively in Figure 6, there is evidence of persistent mass presence.
B) The mass in the right upper lobe bronchus is consistent in size between Figure 1a and Figure 3, and post-operatively in Figure 6, there is no evidence of the mass, indicating successful removal.
C) Consolidation is more pronounced in Figure 2 compared to Figure 5, and post-operatively in Figure 6, there is a recurrence of consolidation.
D) The right upper lobe bronchial mass appears smaller in Figure 4 compared to Figure 1b, and post-operatively in Figure 6, there is an indication of residual mass.
E) In Figure 1a, the mass size is unchanged compared to Figure 2, and post-operatively in Figure 6, there is a new mass lesion in the left upper lobe.
F) The consolidation in the right upper lobe is resolved in Figure 6, compared to its presence in Figure 5, with no signs of mass recurrence post-operatively.
